exceptions: Archived ListPlex reference and unchanged external author implementations retain their historical runtime; PARLAY_SEQUENTIAL may be a separately labelled debugging build, never the one-worker speedup denominator.
granularity_policy: Prefer library defaults or a proven structural rule; no dataset-name/hardware lookup tables or per-case tuned task thresholds

gbbs_reference.role: Optional design and implementation reference, not a required dependency or restriction on ideas
gbbs_reference.parlay_dependency_note: GBBS pins a different ParlayLib repository/revision; use the user-selected joey001 fork for candidates and check API compatibility rather than substituting GBBS dependencies.

worker_launch_contract: Set PARLAY_NUM_THREADS before process/runtime initialization for each candidate process
Check observed parlay::num_workers() equals requested workers
Use the same native scheduler build at P=1 and P>1
Do not create a separate scheduler/thread pool inside each root or recursive call
Apply verified process CPU affinity; OMP_PLACES and OMP_PROC_BIND do not bind Parlay workers
